notification.title: How to Jump from a Moving Car

content.text: Hurling yourself from a moving car should be a last resort, for example if your brakes are defective and your car is about to head off a cliff or into a train.
Apply the emergency brake. This may not stop the car, but it might slow it down enough to make jumping safer.

content.headline: Make sure you jump at an angle that will take you out of the path of the car.
content.text: Make sure you jump at an angle that will take you out of the path of the car.

Since your body will be moving at the same velocity as the car, you're going to continue to move in the direction the car is moving. If the car is going straight, try to jump at an angle that will take you away from it.

content.headline: Tuck in your head and your arms and legs.
content.text: Tuck in your head and your arms and legs.

content.headline: Aim for a soft landing site: grass, brush, wood chips, anything but pavement—or a tree.
content.text: Aim for a soft landing site: grass, brush, wood chips, anything but pavement—or a tree.
Stuntpeople wear pads and land in sandpits. You won't have this luxury, but anything that gives a bit when the body hits it will minimize injury.

content.headline: Roll when you hit the ground.
content.text: Roll when you hit the ground.
After you have applied the emergency brake and the car has slowed, open the car door. Jump out at an angle away from the direction in which the car is traveling.

full_text:
Hurling yourself from a moving car should be a last resort, for example if your brakes are defective and your car is about to head off a cliff or into a train.
Apply the emergency brake. This may not stop the car, but it might slow it down enough to make jumping safer.
Open the car door.
Make sure you jump at an angle that will take you out of the path of the car.
Since your body will be moving at the same velocity as the car, you're going to continue to move in the direction the car is moving. If the car is going straight, try to jump at an angle that will take you away from it.
Tuck in your head and your arms and legs.
Aim for a soft landing site: grass, brush, wood chips, anything but pavement—or a tree.
Stuntpeople wear pads and land in sandpits. You won't have this luxury, but anything that gives a bit when the body hits it will minimize injury.
Roll when you hit the ground.
After you have applied the emergency brake and the car has slowed, open the car door. Jump out at an angle away from the direction in which the car is traveling.
